expectations.evidence: Executive summary states 'The platform is built on OpenStack for IaaS' and Section 7 provides detailed OpenStack platform design including Kolla-Ansible deployment, service catalog, HA architecture, and project structure.

Section 4 covers ACI fabric design in depth: spine-leaf topology with Nexus 9000, 3x APIC cluster, detailed tenant model with VRFs/BDs/EPGs (e.g., epg-cde-app, epg-cde-db), contracts table with provider/consumer EPGs and filters, and ACI-OpenStack integration via Cisco ACI Neutron ML2 plugin with OpFlex agent.

Section 6 details Ceph architecture: 6 OSD nodes with BlueStore, pool layout (rbd-vms, rbd-ephemeral, rbd-images, rbd-backups with 3x replication; rgw-default with EC 4+2), CRUSH rules with rack-aware failure domains, and integration with Cinder/Glance/Nova.

Section 11.2 maps all 12 PCI-DSS requirements to specific controls. CDE is isolated in its own ACI VRF with no direct route to corporate VRF, contracts enforce whitelist-only, dm-crypt encryption at rest, immutable logging with 1-year retention, MFA via Keycloak, and two-person approval for CDE changes.

Section 11.3 maps all five SOC2 Trust Service Criteria (Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, Privacy) to specific implementations including HA architecture, encryption, RBAC, audit trails, and data retention policies.

Section 8 details a multi-layer identity architecture: Keycloak as central IdP (OIDC/SAML, MFA), FreeIPA for Linux host identity (LDAP/Kerberos, HBAC, SSH keys), Keystone federated with Keycloak via OIDC, HashiCorp Vault for secrets, and a full RBAC model.

Section 9 specifies Prometheus (HA with Thanos), Grafana dashboards, Loki for log aggregation, Alertmanager with tiered alerting (P1-P4), Wazuh as SIEM/HIDS, and detailed exporter coverage (node_exporter, ceph_exporter, libvirt_exporter, aci_exporter, etc.).

Section 10 covers Ansible via AWX for configuration management, OpenTofu for infrastructure provisioning, Packer for image building, GitLab CI/Gitea Actions for CI/CD pipelines, and includes detailed repository structure, day-2 automation playbooks, and Event-Driven Ansible for automated remediation.

Section 14 defines a 6-person team with specific roles (Platform Lead, 2x OpenStack/Ceph Engineers, Network/Security Engineer, Automation Engineer, Monitoring/SRE), on-call rotation (1 week on / 5 weeks off), and emphasizes >95% automation coverage and cross-training. Design principle #6 states 'Operational simplicity over elegance'.

Section 5.1 specifies 16 compute nodes with 2x AMD EPYC 9454 (48C each), 512GB RAM per node. Includes capacity math: 1,536 physical cores, 8,192 GB total RAM, supporting 500 VMs at ~33-40% utilization with AZ failover headroom. Section 13.1 provides a capacity vs demand table.
